leads.summary: Releasing the inhibitor before orphan cleanup also releases it during a real pacman removal transaction
leads.consequence: On an interactive update with orphans, accepting the confirmation runs sudo pacman -Rns (including package removal hooks) after the sleep/idle/lid inhibitor has been stopped. Closing the lid during this transaction can suspend it, precisely the interrupted-package-transaction case the new lid lock is meant to prevent. On success the update continues to analyze-logs/status/restart; an interrupted transaction has no automatic redo until a later update. The comment 'The package transactions are done' is false for this path. Consider releasing the lid inhibitor for the unbounded question but reacquiring it for confirmed removal, or splitting the confirm and removal phases and keeping inhibition for the latter.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (Q2 side effect); corroborated; published as part of NEW1 suggestion

leads.summary: Current quattro rewrote update lifecycle and inhibitor launcher, the PR conflicts and its EXIT-trap removal cannot be carried over unchanged
leads.location: bin/omarchy-update:59-60 and bin/omarchy-update-stay-awake:106-119 versus quattro tip 5c7cef1e, bin/omarchy-update:73-83,95-97,129-180 and bin/omarchy-update-stay-awake:474-506
leads.consequence: Three-way merge (31bd80d base, 1bb0973 head, 5c7cef1 tip) has conflict markers in all four changed files. Tip uses one hold_command array with --what=sleep:idle, so resolving the old two-branch masks alone does not protect the actual launched command. Tip runs orphan review BEFORE hooks/mise/AUR; moving stop to before the orphan question without relocating/reacquiring it removes lid protection from later AUR transactions. More importantly tip's EXIT trap is cleanup_update, which ends the sudo keepalive and revokes sudo; replacing it with trap - EXIT before the orphan step would omit this cleanup on any failure from orphan/restart/hooks/mise/AUR. Rebase must preserve the cleanup trap and release the inhibitor with tip's update_stay_awake_stopped tracking, while editing the new single hold_command --what. These are conditional integration hazards, not a claim that the currently conflicting PR has been merged or that current head alone executes the tip code.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (Q3); corroborated; published as NEW1

leads.summary: The lid-mask assertion accepts a malformed mask that logind rejects
leads.consequence: The test's grep is a substring match and its systemd-inhibit stub just logs argv then execs sleep. A plausible typo such as --what=sleep:idle:handle-lid-switch-invalid in both branches still passes the added assertion and all three focused suites, but systemd v261's inhibit_what_from_string rejects the extra token and logind returns Invalid what specification. Production redirects inhibitor stderr to /dev/null, so the user can see Stay Awake while no lid/sleep inhibitor is acquired. Match the complete --what argument as a distinct token, or use a validating stub/negative mutant assertion; for a startup-health assertion test that the inhibitor was actually acquired, not just logged.
leads.triage: factual (mutant ran in Sol sandbox); not published: speculative test hardening, and the test must be rewritten on quattro

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12419#issuecomment-5831035675) and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12419#issuecomment-5847173320), checked at `1bb09736`.

**Outcome:** both earlier points are resolved at this head. The PR now conflicts with current `quattro`, and there the orphan-prompt fix does not carry over as written. Details follow.

| Earlier point | Status at `1bb09736` |
|---|---|
| Lid lock covers the orphan-package prompt | Resolved |
| Test covers only the `else` branch of `start()` | Resolved |
| #10205 makes the same `--what` change | Still applies (#10205 is open) |

**Verified:**
- `omarchy-update-stay-awake stop` and `trap - EXIT` now run after `omarchy-update-mise` and before `omarchy-update-orphan-pkgs`. The orphan prompt now runs after both the inhibitor and the update's Stay Awake idle marker are released. Restoring the previous ordering makes `update-lock-test.sh` fail ("orphan prompt ran while the update still held the lid lock") and `update-sequence-test.sh` fail its order check.
- The `--what` assertion now runs directly and under `omarchy-update-lock run`. Reverting the mask on only the `OMARCHY_UPDATE_LOCK_FD` branch fails with "(locked launch)", and reverting only the `else` branch fails with "(direct launch)". The previous head's test still passed that locked-branch-only revert, so the gap was real, and the new test catches it.
- `update-lock-test.sh`, `update-sequence-test.sh` and `bin-style-test.sh` pass on this head.
- The earlier logind statement still holds for systemd v261.2 (Omarchy stable) and v262. The relevant logind sources are identical between the two.

One correction to the reply: `omarchy-update-analyze-logs` and `omarchy-update-status` previously ran inside the lock (before `stop`). They now run outside it. That change is harmless, but they did not run "without the lock as before".

### Rebasing onto current `quattro` needs a different orphan-step fix

GitHub reports the PR as conflicting, and a three-way merge against the `quattro` tip conflicts in all four changed files. Beyond the text, `quattro` changed the update order on purpose:

```text
quattro bin/omarchy-update (tip)
  stay-awake start
  system-pkgs, migrate
  orphan-pkgs              <- gum confirm, no timeout, still reached under -y
  analyze-logs, status
  restart --services-only
  hook post-update, mise
  AUR (yay)
  stay-awake stop          <- after AUR, deliberately
  restart --reboot-only
```

Commit 13a4306a keeps the inhibitor through hooks, mise and AUR builds, and `test/shell.d/update-hook-security-test.sh` asserts that order.

**Impact:** neither direct port works.
- **Keep this PR's shape** (stop before the orphan step): hooks, mise and AUR builds run uninhibited. In an isolated sandbox with stubs, this makes `update-sequence-test.sh` and `update-hook-security-test.sh` fail.
- **Port only the `--what` mask:** the lid issue from the earlier review returns. The orphan prompt now sits in the middle of the lid-locked window.
- **Carry `trap - EXIT` over:** on `quattro` the EXIT trap is `cleanup_update`, which also ends the sudo keepalive and revokes the sudo timestamp. Clearing it early would skip that cleanup on later failures.

**Suggested change:** when rebasing:
- **The mask:** it becomes a single edit to the shared `hold_command` in `bin/omarchy-update-stay-awake` (`/usr/bin/systemd-inhibit --what=sleep:idle`). The inhibitor has one launch command there, so one assertion covers every launch path.
- **The tests:** they need to redirect the absolute `/usr/bin/systemd-inhibit`, as `quattro`'s tests do (through `sudo-boundary-test.sh` or a `sed` rewrite), because a PATH-only stub is not reached. `quattro`'s `update-lock-test.sh` also renames the state directory, so the orphan guard, if copied unchanged, would never fail.
- **The orphan prompt:** handle it without moving `stop`. For `-y` runs there is a precedent: `quattro`'s `omarchy-update-restart` already reports and moves on under `OMARCHY_UPDATE_UNATTENDED=1`, and `docs/update-process.md` already says orphan removal does the same under `-y`, which `omarchy-update-orphan-pkgs` does not yet do. That covers unattended runs only. An interactive run still reaches the prompt, so a bounded prompt or releasing only the lid part around the question would cover that case. Either way, keeping the confirmed `sudo pacman -Rns` removal inhibited would keep that transaction protected. At this head it runs with no inhibitor at all, where before this PR it ran under `sleep:idle`.
- **Docs:** update the flow in `docs/update-process.md` to match whichever shape lands. At this head it still shows `stop` after status.

These directions come from the source only. No implementation was tested.

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of this head, the previous head, the PR fork point and the `quattro` tip, plus systemd v261.2 and v262 logind sources. The head's `update-lock-test.sh`, `update-sequence-test.sh` and `bin-style-test.sh` ran in an isolated sandbox with stubbed `systemd-inhibit`, `sudo`, `pkexec` and update steps, along with per-branch and ordering mutants. A separate check ran the real `omarchy-update-orphan-pkgs` with stubbed `pacman` and `gum`. On `quattro`, `update-sequence-test.sh` and `update-hook-security-test.sh` ran as-is and with the stop moved. `quattro`'s `update-lock-test.sh` could not run in the sandbox, so conclusions about it come from source. No real logind, polkit, lid hardware or package transactions were exercised.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
